required_fields: run id; branch; delay; delay mode; sample index; retained/throwaway status; q50 inclusion; typed character
why_required: Anchors every OS/browser counter sample to the same retained key that contributes to the benchmark q50.
current_state: Partial: raw key timing exists in benchmark artifacts, but the compact CPU/QoS rows do not yet carry stable retained-key join ids.
failure_mode_if_missing: Root counters can only be compared as class medians, which is too weak for a mechanism claim.

required_fields: keydown/keypress/keyup enqueue times; EventDispatch start/end; browser monotonic clock; host wall-clock mapping
why_required: Separates queueing or wakeup changes from listener-duration changes and makes sampled counters overlap the measured slice.
current_state: Partial: Chromium traces have EventDispatch slices, but they are not currently joined to OS-counter sample ids.
failure_mode_if_missing: A fast row could be misread as faster JS work when only input enqueue or wakeup timing moved.

required_fields: helper pid; process group; launch/start/end; command; nice/taskpolicy/QoS policy; CPU duration; exit status
why_required: The decisive local split is policy-sensitive CPU: ordinary/utility rows are fast while background/maintenance rows stay slow.
current_state: Partial: helper mode names are recorded, but per-retained-key PID, lifetime, and effective policy are not.
failure_mode_if_missing: The observed fast/slow split could be joined to the wrong helper or wrong policy window.

required_fields: renderer pid; browser pid; main thread id if available; page target/frame id; browser revision
why_required: Process-level counters need to identify the foreground renderer that handled the measured input.
current_state: Partial: browser revision and trace target exist in some artifacts; renderer pid/thread id is not a stable sidecar field.
failure_mode_if_missing: Powermetrics or trace samples may describe the wrong process or aggregate away the foreground renderer.

required_fields: collector run id; powermetrics plist path; trace file path; sample begin/end; sample id; notification ids; sample interval
why_required: Turns privileged sampled counters into per-key evidence instead of a run-level correlation.
current_state: Missing: current artifacts do not record collector filenames, sample ids, or trace notifications.
failure_mode_if_missing: Counter rows cannot be audited against individual retained keys or source-span windows.

required_fields: with/without collector control rows; collector pid; collector CPU; dropped samples; class-order preservation
why_required: Root collectors and browser tracing can perturb exactly the scheduler and power state under test.
current_state: Partial: existing no-trace/trace controls cover some browser-trace effects, but not root counter overhead.
failure_mode_if_missing: A counter-backed mechanism could be an artifact of the observer changing the class ordering.

required_fields: AC/battery state; low-power mode; thermal pressure; OS build; core counts; container state; browser build
why_required: Power and scheduler hypotheses are host-state sensitive and need portability context.
current_state: Partial: local host metadata is in the report, but not in a per-run sidecar schema.
failure_mode_if_missing: Runs from different host states can be pooled as if they were equivalent.

required_fields: Gutenberg source-span ids; V8 slices; task queue ids; protocol command timing; scheduler trace categories
why_required: Needed only if OS counters do not explain the split and the claim moves to Chromium scheduler state.
current_state: Partial: Gutenberg source spans exist; scheduler/runtime categories are not in the compact counter run.
failure_mode_if_missing: Browser-scheduler explanations would be unjoinable to the measured input windows.
